On Mon, Nov 1, 2026 at 10:05 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Rishi / Laura — looping you in. ACME is pushing back on our gross negligence carve-out.

Team — quick take and two paths we can propose back. TL;DR: recommended compromise is Option B (uncapped only for proven willful misconduct/fraud; gross negligence capped but with a materiality threshold).

Option A — Redwood-first stance:
- Carve out for "willful misconduct or fraud" remains uncapped and defined as intentional or deliberate wrongdoing proven by clear and convincing evidence.
- Gross negligence treated as "no greater than negligence" and remains subject to the overall contract cap (e.g., 2x fees or $5M whichever greater). This is close to what procurement wants but raises pushback risk from ACME legal.

Option B — Compromise (recommended):
- Willful misconduct and fraud: uncapped carve-out, subject to "clear and convincing evidence" standard and limited to acts by officers or senior employees acting within scope of employment.
- Gross negligence: carve-out only if it results in a material breach of the MSA that directly causes the claimed damages AND exceeds a demonstrable monetary threshold (propose $250,000 or 0.5% of the annual contract value, whichever is greater). Otherwise, gross negligence damages are subject to the agreed cap (2x fees / $5M floor).
- Add explicit definitions: "Material breach" means a breach that substantially frustrates the purpose of the agreement after notice and failure to cure within 60 days. "Gross negligence" means a reckless disregard for foreseeable harm, not merely an error of judgment.

Why B: preserves our operational protections while giving ACME a bright-line floor for meaningful harms. The monetary threshold prevents small-value disputes from being uncapped. The evidentiary standard for willful misconduct/fraud narrows risk of speculative claims.

Draft redline snippet I suggest (for their redline doc):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, liability for proven willful misconduct or fraud shall not be limited by the foregoing cap; provided that such conduct is established by clear and convincing evidence. Gross negligence shall be excluded from the cap only where such gross negligence constitutes a material breach of this Agreement and results in damages in excess of $250,000 or 0.5% of the annual Contract Value, whichever is greater. For the avoidance of doubt, indemnification obligations for third-party claims and breaches of confidentiality are separately provided and not subject to the foregoing limitation."

If we want to be firmer we can raise the threshold to $500k or tie to a multiple of annual fees. Let me know how commercial wants to position — I recommend starting at $250k/0.5% and moving up if ACME pushes.

Rishi

Subject: Proposed compromise language for liability carve-outs

Allison — thanks for the quick turn. We discussed internally and would like to propose the following compromise for your legal team to review. We think it addresses Acme’s procurement concerns while protecting both parties from low-value uncapped exposure.

Proposed (compromise) redline:
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, liability arising from proven willful misconduct or fraud shall not be subject to the limitation of liability set forth herein; provided that such misconduct is established by clear and convincing evidence. Gross negligence shall be excluded from the foregoing limitation only if (i) such gross negligence constitutes a material breach of this Agreement and (ii) the damages claimed resulting therefrom exceed the greater of $250,000 or 0.5% of the Contract Value for the then-current 12-month period. For clarity, routine negligence and ordinary contract breaches remain subject to the limitation of liability. Indemnification obligations and claims for breaches of confidentiality or IP infringement shall be addressed separately and may be exempt from these limitations as set forth elsewhere in this Agreement"

Can you confirm whether your team can accept that structure? If not, what is your minimum acceptable monetary threshold (or alternative formulation)? If you want a higher threshold (e.g., $500k) we can discuss escalation to our VP of Legal.

Next step: if you and your counsel agree in principle we’ll incorporate this into the redline for signature.

Thanks — Soojin
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Soojin — appreciate the clear proposal and quick turnaround. Our GC has reviewed and is willing to accept a split approach with the following adjustments:

- Willful misconduct / fraud: Accept uncapped carve-out but require the following language re: proof: "established by clear and convincing evidence and resulting from intentional acts by an officer, director or other person with managerial authority."
- Gross negligence: ACME will accept exclusion from the cap only where damages exceed the greater of $350,000 or 1.0% of the annual Contract Value (we prefer a slightly higher floor than your proposal).
- We also ask that any definition of "material breach" include a 30-day cure period (instead of 60) for customer-facing outages.

If Redwood can accept the $350k / 1% floor and the 30-day cure, we can proceed to incorporate these edits and move to execution.
